_about: The facts admission of the vehicle facts API (src/facts, GET/POST /api/facts/v1): which open-data offers (src/open_data/offers.py, status `offered`) become facts in a `vehicle-facts/1` record. Separate from the run allowlist data/open_data_admission.json (runs stay in shadow). An offer becomes a fact only when an entry names its (source, field, route), the match level reaches min_level and every `require` holds; everything else is withheld (owner diagnostics, never in the record). `field` is the offer field name of data/open_datasets.json field_map; `named` is the descriptive name the PR used. `require` is a list, or {wltp: [...], nedc: [...]} chosen by the target's cycle (match.nedc_target: an EEA NEDC registration year). Reviewer-edited data: the code infers nothing beyond it.

requires.all_survivors_agree: every surviving row that states the value states the same value (offer identified_by unique | all_survivors_agree)
requires.co2_selected: the source's exact subset was narrowed by an exact co2_wltp match (exact_subset basis type_code+co2 | co2)
requires.type_code_match: the source's candidates are the rows carrying the government type code (match type_code.status match)

_require_cycles: E3: `require` per target cycle. wltp: a WLTP registration year whose government row states co2_wltp; nedc: an EEA NEDC registration year (match.nedc_target); wltp_no_gov_co2: a WLTP year whose government row has no co2_wltp (match co2_key `unavailable`), where co2_selected is impossible: only an entry naming this cycle uses it (curb_weight_kg: the type-code identity, the rule NEDC years already use, plus the E1 / E2 rules), and its fact's basis reads `type_code_match (no government CO2)`. Every other entry falls back to its wltp list: fuel / energy consumption keep co2_selected strictly (consumption depends on the configuration, and without the government CO2 there is no selector). Wheelbase never required co2_selected.

agreement._about: E2 (reviewed, 2026-10-09): survivors of these sources agree on a field of `fields` when the spread (max - min) of their values is within the field's published precision: `spread` (the field's unit) and, when set, `spread_pct` % of the median. The returned value is the lower median of one value per configuration row (no registration weights: the EEA shards store none), rounded to `round`. A fact admitted under a non-zero spread carries agreement {rule: within_precision, spread, n_values (distinct values)}; an exact agreement carries none (byte-identical records). Anything wider stays withheld (offer_survivors_disagree). A field not listed (wheelbase_mm, electric_range_km) agrees only exactly. `row_range` (fields whose EEA value is a median between MIN and MAX, range_policy equal_only): a row whose own MAX - MIN is within it counts with its stored value; a wider row, or one whose MIN or MAX is outside the E1 band, loses only its own value (row_range_dropped, debug only); when more than row_range_max_share of the survivors lose it that way the offer is withheld as offer_range (no fact from a mostly-ranged set). Without row_range a row with MIN != MAX withholds the offer (offer_range) as before.

never.reason: SAE luggage volume (cu ft), not the VDA cargo definition
US / Canadian test cycle, not comparable with WLTP
an American-source gearbox for a European-approval target
CVS dimensions for a European-approval target
an ADEME catalogue outside the target's period

government_overlap._about: Government wins: an open-data column the government row also states is never returned. A survivor row of an offer's source that states a different value is counted in withheld as contradicts_government (diagnostics only).
